## Child Analysis

```{r}
#| label: packages
# TODO: Pin versions in knitted output for reproducability
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
```

Okay let's take a look at our data.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

DATA_DIR <- "data"

# I know double-assignment like this is bad form but I need the long names
#  for code readability and the short names for code debug-ability
english_baseline_df <- en_bl <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "ENGLISH_Child Baseline Data.sav"))
english_control_df <- en_c <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "ENGLISH_Child Follow-Up - Control.sav"))
english_treatment_df <- en_tx <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "ENGLISH_Child Follow-Up - Experimental.sav"))
spanish_baseline_df <- es_bl <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "SPANISH_Child Baseline Data.sav"))
spanish_baseline_2_df <- es_bl2 <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "SPANISH 2_Child Baseline Data.sav"))
spanish_control_df <- es_c <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "SPANISH_Child Follow-Up - Control.sav"))
spanish_treatment_df <- es_tx <- read_sav(file.path(DATA_DIR, "SPANISH_Child Follow-Up - Experimental.sav"))
```

```{r}
COLUMN_CSV_DIR = "column_names"

tibble(
  new_name = "",
  old_name = names(es_tx),
  label = map_chr(es_tx, ~ attr(.x, "label"))
) %>% write_csv(file.path(COLUMN_CSV_DIR, "spanish_treatment_columns.csv"))

```

```{r}
# NOTE: this is not something I will ship. This is bizarre, it's just faster
#  for me to edit. It should be an R document.

# --- Helper Functions ---------------------------------------------------------
#' Given a dataframe, will rename the columns of that dataframe
#' according to the new_name and old_name columns of the supplied CSV.
.rename_columns_from_file <- function(data, csv_filepath) {
  column_mapping <- read_csv(
    filename,
    col_names = TRUE,
    col_types = cols(
      name = col_character(),
      old_name = col_character(),
    ),
    col_select = all_of(c("new_name", "old_name"))
  )

  return(data %>%
    rename(!!!setNames(column_mapping$old_name, column_mapping$new_name)))
}


```

```{r}
dfs <- list(
  en_bl = english_baseline_df,
  en_c = english_control_df,
  en_tx = english_treatment_df,
  es_bl = spanish_baseline_df,
  es_bl2 = spanish_baseline_2_df,
  es_c = spanish_control_df,
  es_tx = spanish_treatment_df
  )

sapply(dfs, ncol)
```
